gloss: magma; molten rock beneath the earth's surface

definitions.gloss: magma; molten rock beneath the earth's surface
definitions.explanation: Extremely hot molten rock found deep beneath the earth's surface, particularly under volcanoes. When it reaches the surface during an eruption, it is called 溶岩 (lava).

examples.japanese: マグマが{地表|ちひょう}に{出|で}ると{溶岩|ようがん}になる。
examples.english: When magma reaches the surface, it becomes lava.

examples.japanese: {火山|かざん}の{地下|ちか}にはマグマが{溜|た}まっている。
examples.english: Magma has accumulated beneath the volcano.

examples.japanese: マグマの{温度|おんど}は{千度|せんど}を{超|こ}えることもあり、{地殻|ちかく}の{変動|へんどう}に{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}える。
examples.english: The temperature of magma can exceed 1,000 degrees and has a major impact on crustal movement.

notes:
A loanword from English (ultimately from Latin/Greek). Refers to molten rock found beneath the earth's surface. When magma erupts and flows on the surface, it is called {溶岩|ようがん} (lava). An essential term for understanding volcanoes, which are a major part of Japan's geography and natural disaster awareness.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- マグマが{上昇|じょうしょう}する: magma rises
- マグマが{噴出|ふんしゅつ}する: magma erupts
- マグマ{溜|だ}まり: magma chamber
- マグマの{活動|かつどう}: magmatic activity

RELATED WORDS:
- {溶岩|ようがん} — lava (magma after it reaches the surface)
- {火山|かざん} — volcano
- {噴火|ふんか} — volcanic eruption
- マントル — mantle (the layer below the crust)
